text:
Abu Dhabi's sovereign fund ADIA put $500 million into Lenskart in 2023 for about a 10% stake. Gulf capital is now a serious force in Indian startups.

But you do not need to be Lenskart-sized to tap it. Abu Dhabi accelerators, Dubai angel funds and India-focused Gulf VCs now write cheques from pre-seed onwards.

In this carousel: 8 Middle East investors that back Indian founders, from Hub71 and AUM Ventures to ADIA and QIA, with stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: start with the programmes, not the sovereign funds. Hub71 and similar accelerators are the open door at pre-seed to Series A, and Gulf investors care a lot about your plan for the GCC market. Show a real reason to expand there, not just a slide.

Save this for your next raise.

investors.name: BeyondSeed
investors.note: Launched Global Angel Fund I from Dubai in 2026 to pool Gulf angel money into India.

investors.name: AUM Ventures
investors.reach: No public form · warm intro via its India team
investors.note: Fund II targets ₹750 Cr for 25–30 Indian deep-tech startups; offices in Bengaluru and Mumbai.

investors.name: Gulf Islamic Investments
investors.note: Runs $300M+ India Growth funds. Good fit for D2C brands eyeing GCC expansion.

investors.name: Investcorp (India PE)
investors.note: Plans 2–3 India deals a year. A name to know once you reach scale.

investors.name: Mubadala
investors.note: Also the backer of Hub71, so its accelerator is the early-stage door.

investors.name: ADIA
investors.note: Its $200M Meril deal was the only Gulf cheque among India's top 2025 rounds.

investors.name: Qatar Investment Authority
investors.note: Writes growth cheques only. Build the relationship once you are at scale.

text:
Prosus, a Dutch-listed company, has invested about $8.6 billion in Indian startups and has been on Swiggy's cap table since 2017. Europe has quietly become one of India's biggest sources of startup capital.

And it is moving earlier. European funds now write pre-seed and seed cheques into Indian AI, deep tech and consumer startups, many with Bengaluru teams.

In this carousel: 8 European investors that back Indian founders, from Entrepreneur First and Picus Capital to Bertelsmann and British International Investment, with stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: check their recent Indian deals first and pitch the partner who did them. Many European funds back Indian startups only through a co-investor, so a warm intro from an Indian VC they already work with often beats a cold email.
